sections.overview: This geometrid moth occurs patchily in Eurasian wetlands.
sections.identification: Its golden forewings carry an oblique silver-white line edged with tawny; wingspan is about 22–40 mm.
sections.habitat: It inhabits fens, marshes, bogs and waterlogged or overgrown meadows.
sections.diet: Larvae feed on wetland plants such as yellow loosestrife and bog myrtle, and sometimes dock.
sections.behavior: Adults are mainly active at dusk and night; the caterpillar overwinters.
sections.reproduction: It has one or two generations yearly, varying with latitude.
sections.ecology: The genus Chariaspilates currently has a single described species, so it has no direct congener comparison.
sections.conservation: Its conservation status is not uniformly assessed across its range, so regional categories should not be treated as a global result.
